c.tagline: Zambia's gateway to Victoria Falls, where the Zambezi thunders into the mist.

taxi.fareNote: There is no Uber or Bolt in Livingstone and taxis are unmetered — agree the fare before getting in. Most visitors use lodge-arranged transfers or booked activity operators rather than hailing on the street.

emergency.note: 112 also reaches emergency services from most mobile phones; response times can be slow, and many visitors rely on their lodge or a private clinic first.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Don't walk the road to the Falls or along the Zambezi at dusk — elephants roam freely, and petty theft occurs around the market.

hood_desc: The compact grid along Mosi-oa-Tunya Road with the Livingstone Museum, Mukuni Park curio market, banks, restaurants and most backpacker lodges; the convenient walkable base for first-timers.
The lush strip of luxury lodges lining the Zambezi upstream of the falls, home to sunset cruises, spa resorts and riverfront game lawns; best for travellers wanting comfort and calm on the water.

The southern gateway toward the Mosi-oa-Tunya (Victoria Falls) National Park entrance and the Zambezi rainforest, dotted with safari lodges and activity operators for rafting, bungee and Devil's Pool.
A traditional township east of the centre around the Maramba market and the Maramba Cultural Museum, with local eateries, drumming and dance; an authentic, budget-friendly, less touristy feel.
A quiet residential suburb of guesthouses and self-catering homes north of the centre, good for families and longer stays wanting a relaxed local pace away from the tourist strip.
lodging: The Royal Livingstone Victoria Falls Hotel by Anantara
The David Livingstone Safari Lodge & Spa

water.note: Town supply is chlorinated but quality varies — most visitors stick to bottled or filtered water.

transit.hours: Shared minibuses run roughly 6:00 AM to early evening; after dark you rely on taxis or a prearranged transfer.
transit.note: Livingstone has no metro, tram or city bus network. Shared minibuses ply the main routes cheaply, while taxis and lodge transfers cover the tourist sites and airport.
transit.pay: Minibus and taxi fares are paid in cash (Zambian Kwacha) directly to the driver or conductor; there is no transit card. US dollars are widely accepted for tours and lodges.

bus: Intercity coaches to Lusaka (Mazhandu Family Bus, Shalom) and cross-border services to Botswana, Namibia and Zimbabwe
train: Zambia Railways passenger service to Lusaka (slow, infrequent)

transit.m: Taxi to town centre (~15 min); most lodges offer prearranged airport transfers
Hotel shuttle / prearranged transfer to riverfront lodges (~20 min)

tip.r: ~10% at restaurants is appreciated for good service; tipping safari guides, drivers and porters is customary in the tourism trade.
